text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The attorney-general publishes a bill seeking to ammend the National Social Security Act to convert it into a retirement benefits scheme.
- The commissioner of police is instructed to take decisive and tough measures to eradicate banditry in northern frontier districts.
- Dubai-based Kenyan tycooon Ketan Somaia for a third time defies a summons to appear before the parliamentary public accounts committee.
- Opposition political parties unite in calling for constitional reforms.
- The government complains of the negative attitude the public has towards the police force.
- Non-governmental organisations urge the government to take serious steps towards pre-empting violence in this year's general elections.
- Opposition leader Kenneth Matiba is to visit Kisimu to "assess how the Asian community have monopolised the Kenyan economy" with a view to inciting local people to throw Asians out of the area.
- The government releases a list detailing the distribution of the National Youth Development Fund.
- Elusive, self-exiled February Eighteen Resistance Army commander "Brigadier" Odongo arrives in Kenya and goes underground to attend his mother's burial.
